chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pay back what has been missed from the daytime prayers during the daytime, and what has been missed from the night prayers during the night.' I said: 'Can I pay back two Witr prayers in one night?' He said: 'Yes, pay back Witr always.'
ai.seo_question: How should missed daytime and night prayers be compensated according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of temporal fidelity in Qada, requiring that missed daytime prayers be compensated during daylight hours and night prayers at night, preserving the distinct identity of each prayer's time. He further clarifies that while Witr is a night prayer, one may combine two Witr make-ups in a single night, demonstrating flexibility within the strict temporal framework. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maintaining the chronological integrity of obligatory acts while accommodating practical necessities in ritual compensation.
